findings.message: The state.json hold only applies after the target is resolved and found inside the resolved root. `readSnapshot` (read.ts:31-37) reads approvals from the unresolved `${cwd}/.specclaw/changes/*/state.json`, but `placePath` follows symlinks before the check. If `.specclaw` (or `.specclaw/changes`) is a symlink to a folder outside the project, the resolved target falls outside `root`. `relativeInside` then returns undefined and the gate returns ALLOW (line 44) before the STATE_FILE test runs. The model can then write `approved` into the very file the gate reads, so the self-approval guard the README promises is bypassed. Fix: test the STATE_FILE rule against the path as `readSnapshot` addresses it (the cwd-relative spelling) as well as the resolved target. Alternatively, resolve `.specclaw/changes` once and hold any target under that resolved directory. Add table rows for a `.specclaw` symlink, a `.specclaw/changes` symlink, and a direct path.
findings.scenario: cwd /repo with /repo/.specclaw -> /shared/specclaw and an unapproved change 001-a. Write file_path=/repo/.specclaw/changes/001-a/state.json with content {"phase":"build","phases":{"proposal":{"status":"approved"}}}. The stat realPath is /shared/specclaw/changes/001-a/state.json, which is outside /repo, so the result is ALLOW in block mode. The next refresh reads the change as approved and every project edit is unlocked.

findings.message: EXEMPT is case-insensitive (`/i`). The comparison runs on resolved real paths, so on a case-sensitive file system a separate folder such as `.Specclaw/` or `.GIT/` is a real project folder, yet it is exempted as if it were `.specclaw/` or `.git/`. The README only exempts `.specclaw/` and `.git/`. Drop `/i` from EXEMPT and keep it on STATE_FILE, where over-holding is safe.
findings.scenario: Linux, block mode, no approved change. Write /repo/.Specclaw/run.sh -> relative '.Specclaw/run.sh' matches EXEMPT -> ALLOW, although the file is a project file outside .specclaw/.

findings.message: In warn mode, `$.ui.toast(verdict.message)` is neither awaited nor caught. If the toast rejects, the rejection is unhandled and the user gets no warning, with nothing to show the warning was not delivered. Await it, or catch it and fall back to status.
findings.scenario: gate=warn, no approved change, ui.toast rejects -> the Write runs, no warning is shown, and an unhandled rejection is raised.
